category_title: Students focused on learning and demonstrating ability with relatively effective self-regulation
minimal_context: The student is working on a geometry assignment in the classroom that involves coloring and marking angles and sides of triangles.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please start your geometry assignment. You need to color and mark the angles and sides of the triangles.

STUDENT: I feel confident about this. I know my success comes from my own effort, as well as the help of my teachers and parents.

TUTOR: Go ahead and begin working.

STUDENT: I am using correction strategies as I go. I made a correct evaluation of the quality of my product on this first triangle, so I am fixing the marks.

TUTOR: What are you going to do for the next one?

STUDENT: (Starts coloring the next triangle immediately) I'm just going to start marking it. Even though I'm trying, my use of learning and self-regulation strategies is still not optimal because my planning is only partial.

options.A: Step out of the classroom to get a drink of water if feeling frustrated by the student.
options.B: Ask the student to describe the form of the next triangle before he begins marking it.
options.C: Withhold attention from the student while he begins coloring the next triangle on the assignment.
options.D: Provide a geometry task modified to fit the student's ability level or below grade level.
